extraction.name: ArtifactsBench
extraction.description: ArtifactsBench is a benchmark of 1,825 diverse tasks for evaluating LLMs on interactive visual code generation. It renders each artifact and captures dynamic behavior via temporal (three-step) screenshots, assessed by a Multimodal LLM-as-Judge guided by fine-grained, per-task checklists. Tasks span nine domains and are stratified by complexity.
extraction.creator: Tencent Hunyuan Team
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Tasks were aggregated from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots. Automated filters were applied, followed by de-duplication, prompt rewriting, difficulty calibration, checklist generation, and solvability validation.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two-stage de-duplication using MinHash + semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS, plus screenshot perceptual hashing. Automated filters drop incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items. Experts rewrite prompts for clarity/completeness/executability; LLM rewriting adds diverse styles; humans verify. Difficulty assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ models.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each query is paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities. Checklists are LLM-drafted (by Hunyuan-Turbos) and then human-refined for specificity and screenability. A 10% manually curated seed anchors calibration and achieves Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8 among annotators; the seed is reused as few-shot references. Items are grouped into five vision-oriented and five code-oriented dimensions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A 10% manually curated seed achieves Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8 among annotators. Human validation used a double-blind protocol on 280 queries and 6 models judged by multiple front-end engineers; the final human ground-truth score represents the median of individual annotators' ratings. Pairwise consistency rate (Pair ACC) was used to quantify agreement.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Multiple engineers with extensive front-end development experience
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Hunyuan-Turbos (checklist generation), Gemini-2.5-Pro (query classification, evaluation referee), Qwen2.5-VL-72B (evaluation referee), Playwright/headless Chromium (artifact execution and screenshot capture)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Dataset specs, checklist templates, evaluation scripts, and referee settings are released. Future work targets richer dynamics beyond discrete screenshots, agentic multi-turn self-debugging, and broader artifact domains.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The discrete screenshot sampling approach may not fully capture the fluidity, correctness, and robustness of highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions. The benchmark currently focuses on single-turn artifact generation and does not assess agentic or iterative development capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluation of LLMs on interactive visual code generation tasks; testing and ranking LLMs across diverse domains (games, SVG, web applications, simulations, data science, management systems, multimedia editing, quick tools); fine-grained capability analysis across difficulty tiers and task categories.

name.evidence: We introduce ArtifactsBench, a benchmark and automated, multimodal evaluation paradigm for visual code generation.

description.evidence: We curate 1,825 diverse tasks and evaluate over 30 leading LLMs. Our automated evaluation achieves 94.4% ranking consistency with WebDev Arena—a de facto gold standard for human preferences in web development—and up to 90.95% pairwise agreement with human experts.

url.evidence: We opensource ArtifactsBench, including the benchmark, evaluation harness, and baseline results at https://artifactsbenchmark.github.io

publisher.evidence: Corresponding Authors: Wiggin Zhou, Tencent; Chayse Zhou, Tencent; Fengzong Lian, Tencent

isLiveDataset.evidence: We release dataset specs, checklist templates, evaluation scripts, and referee settings; future work targets richer dynamics beyond discrete screenshots, agentic multi-turn self-debugging, and broader artifact domains.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: We aggregate candidates from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots. Automated filters drop incomplete, non-visual, license-violating, duplicate, trivial, or non-interactive items, prioritizing dynamics (state changes, animations, responsiveness).

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We aggregate candidates from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We aggregate candidates from expert showcases, open SVG/web-snippet datasets, web case studies, and LLM visual-to-query from screenshots.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Two-stage filtering: (i) MinHash + semantic similarity over prompts, checklists, and normalized DOM/CSS/JS; (ii) screenshot perceptual hashing to catch visually near-identical artifacts. Flagged items are re-authored or discarded. Experts rewrite for clarity/completeness/executability; LLM rewriting adds diverse styles; humans verify. Difficulty is assigned post hoc by aggregated performance of 30+ models to enforce 30%/40%/30%.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Each query is paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities. We LLM-draft and then human-refine for specificity and screenability. A 10% manually curated seed anchors calibration and achieves Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8 among annotators; the seed is reused as few-shot references to keep difficulty high and rubrics consistent.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: A 10% manually curated seed anchors calibration and achieves Cohen's κ ≥ 0.8 among annotators... The process follows a double-blind protocol: annotators remain unaware of the MLLM's scores, and the samples appear in randomized order to mitigate bias. The final human ground-truth score represents the median of the individual annotators' ratings.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: Each query is paired with a 10-dimension checklist covering visual, interactional, and code qualities.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: We randomly selected 280 queries, along with the corresponding data from 6 models, and have them independently scored by multiple engineers with extensive front-end development experience.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: Checklists are generated by Hunyuan-Turbos and human-refined... We use Gemini-2.5-Pro to classify queries... we adopt a dual-referee setup: the open-source Qwen2.5-VL-72B and the proprietary Gemini-2.5-Pro... Execution uses Playwright (headless Chromium) to render artifacts at a resolution of 1024×768.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: We release dataset specs, checklist templates, evaluation scripts, and referee settings; future work targets richer dynamics beyond discrete screenshots, agentic multi-turn self-debugging, and broader artifact domains.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: for highly complex, long-horizon, or state-dependent interactions (e.g., multi-step user workflows in a web application, or the nuanced physics in a game), this discrete sampling may not fully capture the fluidity, correctness, and robustness of the entire interactive experience... ArtifactsBench currently focuses on evaluating the quality of the final artifact generated in a single turn from a given prompt. This scope does not assess an LLM's capability to function as an autonomous agent that can iteratively refine an artifact based on feedback.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We opensource ArtifactsBench, including the benchmark, evaluation harness, and baseline results at https://artifactsbenchmark.github.io, to provide the community with a scalable and accurate tool to accelerate the development of user-centric generative models.
